title: Chosen-Plaintext vs. Chosen-Ciphertext Security of Reduced-Round AES
summary: A nontrivial 5-round AES distinguisher is known only in chosen-ciphertext mode; whether reduced-round AES has different security margins in the two attack settings remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: A nontrivial distinguisher is known for 5-round AES in the secret-key setting, but it can only be constructed in chosen-ciphertext mode. Determine whether the security margin of round-reduced AES, particularly 5-round AES, actually differs between chosen-plaintext and chosen-ciphertext attacks.

scope.domain: Secret-key cryptanalysis of round-reduced AES using distinguishing attacks.
parameters: AES round count: identifies the round-reduced variant, particularly 5 rounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the security margin of round-reduced AES, particularly 5-round AES, actually differs between chosen-plaintext and chosen-ciphertext attacks.

citations.label: New Insights on AES-Like SPN Ciphers

progress.summary: The source reports a nontrivial 5-round AES distinguisher in the secret-key, chosen-ciphertext setting. Because the property applies only there, it suggests—but does not settle—that the two attack settings may have different security margins.
citation_labels: Bing Sun et al., New Insights on AES-Like SPN Ciphers
